The Triplet on Roots to be Abandoned by Seeing.
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.

Dependent on a state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing, there arises a state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing, by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … two aggregates.

Dependent on a state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing (*dassanena pahātabbahetuka*), there arises a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by cultivation (*nevadassanena-nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka*) by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*): dependent on the aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing, mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*) arises.

Dependent on a state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing, there arise states whose roots are both to be abandoned by seeing and neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by cultivation by way of root-condition: [dependent on] the state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing... [and so forth].

Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … [and so on] … Dependent on a state with root-cause to be abandoned by cultivation, a state with root-cause to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of root-condition: dependent on one aggregate with root-cause to be abandoned by cultivation, three aggregates arise … two aggregates … [and so on].

Dependent on a state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka*), a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by cultivation arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*): dependent on the aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation, mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*) arises.

Dependent on a state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation, states whose roots are both to be abandoned by cultivation and neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by cultivation arise by way of the root condition: [dependent on] the state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation...

Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … [and so on] … Dependent on a state with root-cause that is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation,

a state with root-cause that is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation arises by way of root-condition: dependent on a state with root-cause that is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation … [and so on].
Dependent on one aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter;
dependent on delusion accompanied by doubt or accompanied by restlessness, there arises mind-produced matter.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, [dependent on] a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation … [and so forth].
Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates and kamma-produced matter arise … two aggregates … dependent on the aggregates, the physical basis arises;
dependent on the physical basis, the aggregates arise. Dependent on one great primary … dependent on the great primaries, mind-originated matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter arise.

Dependent on a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation, a state whose root is to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root-condition: dependent on delusion accompanied by doubt, the associated aggregates arise.

Dependent on a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation, a state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of root-condition: dependent on delusion accompanied by restlessness, the associated aggregates arise.

dependent on delusion accompanied by doubt, the associated aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.
Dependent on a state rooted in a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation,
there arise states rooted both in a cause to be abandoned by cultivation and in a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation, by way of root condition:
dependent on restlessness-accompanied delusion, there arise the associated aggregates and mind-produced matter.

Dependent on a state whose root is to be abandoned by vision and a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation, a state whose root is to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root-condition:
dependent on one aggregate accompanied by doubt and delusion, three aggregates arise; ... pe ... dependent on two aggregates and delusion, two aggregates arise.

Dependent on a state whose root is to be abandoned by vision and a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation, there arises a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation, by way of root-condition:
dependent on the aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned by vision and the great elements, mind-produced matter arises; [dependent on] the [aggregates] associated with doubt...
Mental-concomitant matter arises dependent on the aggregates and delusion.

[This is] the state with root-cause to be abandoned by seeing, and the state with root-cause neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by cultivation.

[Conditioned by] a state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation and a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation...

Dependent on [states] whose roots are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation, a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation arises by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*):
dependent on aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation and the great elements (*mahābhūta*), mind-originated matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*) arises.

Condition by way of proximity condition: each preceding delusion accompanied by doubt is a condition for each succeeding aggregate accompanied by doubt by way of proximity condition;

each preceding delusion accompanied by restlessness is related to each subsequent aggregate accompanied by restlessness by way of proximity condition; [likewise], advertence is related to states whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation...
[It is] a condition for the aggregates by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation is a condition,
by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*), for a state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation and for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation:
namely, each preceding delusion accompanied by restlessness is a condition for each subsequent aggregate accompanied by restlessness.

It is a condition for delusion by way of proximity-condition; advertence accompanied by restlessness is a condition for the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and for delusion by way of proximity-condition.
States with roots eradicated by vision and states with roots neither eradicated by vision nor by cultivation...
A state whose root is to be abandoned by vision is a condition for a state whose root is to be abandoned by vision by way of proximity condition:
preceding aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are a condition for succeeding aggregates accompanied by doubt by way of proximity condition.
States whose roots are both to be abandoned by vision and neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation...
A state whose roots are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is related to a state whose roots are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation by way of proximity condition:
preceding aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are related to succeeding delusion by way of proximity condition;
aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are related to emergence by way of proximity condition.

States with roots to be abandoned by vision and states with roots neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation are related to a state with a root to be abandoned by vision and a state with a root neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation by way of proximity condition:
preceding aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are related to succeeding [aggregates].
It is a condition for subsequent aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion by way of proximity-condition.

States with roots eradicated by cultivation and states with roots neither eradicated by vision nor by cultivation are conditions for a state with roots eradicated by cultivation by way of proximity-condition ... three. (The progression is the same as for vision.)

by way of the condition of co-nascence … it is a condition, by way of the condition of mutuality.
… is a condition by way of dependence-condition (*nissayapaccaya*) … Strong-dependence:
A state rooted in a cause to be abandoned by vision is a condition, by way of strong-dependence-condition, for a state rooted in a cause to be abandoned by vision.
Condition: object-strong-dependence, proximity-strong-dependence, natural strong-dependence... [etc. ... Natural strong-dependence:
depending on lust rooted in causes to be abandoned by vision, one kills a living being... [etc. ... one causes a schism in the Saṅgha.
Depending on hatred rooted in causes to be abandoned by vision, delusion, wrong view, or aspiration, one kills a living being... [etc. ... one causes a schism in the Saṅgha.

Lust, hatred, delusion, wrong view, and longing rooted in factors to be abandoned by vision are related to lust, [hatred, delusion, wrong view, and] longing rooted in factors to be abandoned by vision ...
[and so on] ... by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A state rooted in factors to be abandoned by vision is related to a state whose roots are neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation ... [and so on].
Condition by way of decisive support (upanissaya-paccaya): proximate decisive support, natural decisive support, etc. Natural decisive support:
relying on lust rooted in the causes to be abandoned by vision, one gives a gift... [and so on] ...one arouses meditative attainment.
Relying on hatred rooted in the causes to be abandoned by vision... delusion... wrong view... longing, one gives a gift... [and so on] ...one arouses meditative attainment.

It causes [these] to arise. A state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing (*dassanena pahātabbahetuka*) is related to lust … craving … aspiration … faith … wisdom … bodily pleasure, bodily pain, the attainment of fruition (*phalasamāpatti*), and delusion by way of the decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing is related to a state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing and to a state that is neither-rooted-in-seeing-nor-rooted-in-cultivation (*nevadassanena-nabhāvanāya*) … [and so forth].

And it is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state whose root is to be abandoned: as immediate decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakata-upanissaya*) ... [etc] ... Natural decisive support:

lust, hatred, delusion, wrong view, and aspiration rooted in the roots to be abandoned by seeing, are conditions, by way of decisive support condition, for the aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion.

A state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka) is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya), for a state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation:
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, natural decisive support … [etc. … Natural decisive support:
lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, or longing whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for [a state] whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation.
[It is] a condition for lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, and longing by way of decisive-support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state rooted in causes to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state rooted in causes to be abandoned by vision by way of decisive-support condition—namely, object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [etc. … Natural decisive support: a state rooted in causes to be abandoned by cultivation … [etc. … is a condition … by way of natural decisive support.
Depending on lust as a decisive support, one kills a living being … [and so on] … one causes a schism in the Saṅgha.
Depending on hatred to be abandoned by cultivation, delusion … conceit … or longing as a decisive support, one kills a living being … [and so on] … one causes a schism in the Saṅgha.
Lust to be abandoned by cultivation … [and so on] … longing is related to lust to be abandoned by vision, and to hatred … [and so on] … by way of decisive support.
… delusion … view … aspiration is related to [its] subsequent state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

Desire-and-lust for one’s own property is related to desire-and-lust for another’s property by way of decisive support condition. Desire-and-lust for what is possessed by oneself is related to desire-and-lust for what is possessed by another by way of decisive support condition.

A state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka) is a condition, by way of decisive support (upanissaya-paccaya), for a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation (nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka)—namely, as immediate decisive support (anantarūpanissaya) and natural decisive support (pakatūpanissaya)… [etc. … Natural decisive support:
relying on lust whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation, one gives a gift… [etc. … one arouses meditative attainment (samāpatti). Regarding cultivation…
Taking as a decisive support (upanissaya) hatred whose cause is to be abandoned by means of development, or delusion, or conceit, or aspiration, one gives a gift... pe ... and arouses an attainment.
Greed whose cause is to be abandoned by means of development... pe ... and aspiration are related to faith... pe ...
to wisdom, to bodily pleasure, to bodily pain, to the attainment of fruition, and to delusion, by way of the condition of decisive support.

A state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka) is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya), for a state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing (dassanena pahātabbahetuka) and for a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by cultivation (nevadassanena-nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka). As natural decisive support (pakatūpanissaya):

lust whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation ... down to ... aspiration (patthanā) is a condition, by way of decisive support condition, for the aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion (moha).

A state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka) is a condition, by way of decisive support (upanissaya-paccaya), for a state whose root is both to be abandoned by cultivation and neither-to-be-abandoned-by-vision-nor-by-cultivation.
[This includes] immediate decisive support (anantarūpanissaya) and natural decisive support (pakatūpanissaya). … Natural decisive support:
lust whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation … [and so on] … aspiration (patthanā) is a condition for states accompanied by restlessness (uddhacca-sahagata).
The aggregates and delusion are related to [their respective states] by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is related to a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition—
namely, object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*), proximity-decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*), and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*).
… [as before] … Natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*): Relying on faith (*saddhā*), one gives a gift … [as before] … one arouses meditative attainment (*samāpatti*).

[One relies on] virtue … [as before] … wisdom (*paññā*) … bodily pleasure (*kāyika-sukha*) … bodily pain (*kāyika-dukkha*) … climate (*utu*) … food (*bhojana*) … lodging (*senāsana*) … Relying on delusion (*moha*), one gives a gift … [as before] … faith … [as before] … Delusion [is the support] for faith … [as before] … for the attainment of fruition (*phala-samāpatti*) … for delusion.
And it is a condition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A state rooted in a cause to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation is a condition for a state rooted in a cause to be abandoned by seeing by way of decisive support condition— that is,
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural-decisive support.
… [as before] … Natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*): Relying on faith (*saddhā*), one adopts wrong views.

[Relying on] virtue (*sīla*) … [as before] … wisdom (*paññā*) … bodily pleasure (*kāyika-sukha*) … bodily pain (*kāyika-dukkha*) … [as before] … lodging (*senāsana*). Relying on delusion (*moha*), one kills living beings … [as before] … one causes a schism in the Saṅgha.
Faith … [as before] … and lodging, as well as delusion, are the conditions for lust (*rāga*) whose root is to be abandoned by vision (*dassanena pahātabba-hetuka*) … [as before] …

A state rooted in a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is related to a state rooted in a cause to be abandoned by cultivation by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). This includes: object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support. A wish (*patthanā*) is related [to its fulfillment] by way of decisive support condition. A state rooted in a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is related to a state rooted in a cause to be abandoned by cultivation by way of decisive support condition—namely, as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support.
… [as before] … Natural strong-dependence: depending on faith, one arouses conceit; … [as before] … depending on delusion, one arouses conceit.

Faith … [as before] … and lodging-place, as well as delusion, are related to lust whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation, … [as before] … and to aspiration, by way of the condition of strong-dependence.
A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation is a condition,
by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing and for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation—

namely, as immediate decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakati-upanissaya*) … [as above] … Natural decisive support: faith … wisdom … bodily pleasure … bodily pain … [and so forth].
Suffering ... [and so on] ... lodging-place is related to the aggregates accompanied by delusion and doubt, and to delusion, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state with a root to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is related to a state with a root to be abandoned by cultivation and to a state with a root to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition—namely, as immediate decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*).

Natural strong-dependence condition …pe…. Natural strong-dependence: faith …pe… and the lodging-place are related to the aggregates accompanied by delusion and to delusion by way of strong-dependence condition.
States whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing and states whose roots are neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by cultivation …pe….
A state whose root is to be abandoned by vision is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state whose root is to be abandoned by vision:

as immediate decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [and so on] … Natural decisive support: the aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are a condition, by way of decisive support condition, for lust … [and so on] … and for aspiration that has its root to be abandoned by vision.

States whose roots are to be abandoned by vision and states whose roots are neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation are related to a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*)— namely,

as proximity-decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [as above] … Natural decisive support: the aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are related to faith by way of natural decisive support.
...pe... wisdom ... bodily pleasure, bodily pain, the attainment of fruition, and delusion are related to [their respective states] by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

Furthermore, states rooted in factors to be abandoned by vision, as well as states rooted in factors to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation, [are related to their respective states by way of decisive support condition].

A state whose root is to be abandoned by vision and a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation are related to each other by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*)—
namely, as proximity-decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [as before] … Natural decisive support:
the aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are related to the aggregates accompanied by doubt and to delusion by way of decisive support condition.

States whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation and whose roots are neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation are related to a state whose root is to be abandoned by vision by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). As a natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*):

the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion, as well as delusion itself, are related to lust... pe ...and to the wish-to-do (*patthanā*) which has a root to be abandoned by vision, by way of decisive support condition.

States whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation and states whose roots are neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation are related to a state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*)— namely,

proximity-decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [etc] … Natural decisive support: the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion, as well as delusion itself, are related to [the state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation] by way of natural decisive support.
Lust whose cause is to be abandoned by abandoning is related to [lust] … pe … to aspiration by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

Furthermore, states whose causes are to be abandoned by cultivation and those whose causes are neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation are related to a state whose cause is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition— namely, as immediate decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*).

Natural decisive support … [etc] … Natural decisive support: the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion, as well as delusion itself, are related to faith … [etc] … and to the attainment of fruition, by way of decisive support condition.
States with roots to be abandoned by cultivation and states with roots neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation … [etc].

A state whose root is to be abandoned by vision (*dassanena pahātabba-hetuka*) and a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation (*nevadassanena-nabhāvanāya pahātabba-hetuka*) are related to each other by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

As natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*): the aggregates accompanied by restlessness (*uddhacca-sahagata*) and delusion (*moha*) are related to the aggregates accompanied by doubt (*vicikicchā-sahagata*) and to delusion by way of decisive support condition.

States whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation and whose roots are neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation are related to states whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation and whose roots are neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), namely:
proximity-decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [etc] … Natural decisive support: restlessness-accompanied [states].
The aggregates and delusion are related to the restlessness-accompanied aggregates and to delusion by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

[In the case of] a pre-arisen state rooted in that which is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation, [it is related] to a state rooted in that which is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation...

It is a condition for the Dhamma by way of pre-arising condition (*purejāta-paccaya*): as object-pre-arising (*ārammaṇa-purejāta*) and as base-pre-arising (*vatthu-purejāta*). Regarding object-pre-arising:

one contemplates the eye as impermanent … [and so on] … one contemplates the ear … [and so on] … one contemplates the physical base (*vatthu*) as impermanent … [and so on] … one contemplates with insight.
One sees a visible form with the divine eye; one hears a sound with the divine ear-element. The visible-form base is a condition for eye-consciousness … [and so on] …
The tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-arising condition (*purejāta-paccaya*). As for the pre-arising condition of the physical basis (*vatthupurejāta*):
the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness ... [and so on] ... the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness ... [and so on] ...
the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates rooted in causes to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation, and for delusion, by way of pre-arising condition.

A state whose root is to be abandoned by vision, and not by cultivation, is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned by vision—namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence. Object-prenascence:
the eye … [as appropriate] … one relishes and delights in the base; taking that as object, lust whose root is to be abandoned by vision arises … [as appropriate] …
Wrong view … pe … doubt … pe … sorrow rooted in causes to be abandoned by vision arises. Base-prenascence:
the base is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for the aggregates rooted in causes to be abandoned by vision.
A state not to be abandoned either by vision or by cultivation is a condition, by way of [prenascence], for a state rooted in causes to be abandoned by cultivation.
Condition by way of prenascence condition: object-prenascence and base-prenascence. Object-prenascence:

the eye … [and so on] … one relishes and delights in the base; taking that as object, greed rooted in what is to be abandoned by cultivation arises, restlessness arises, and grief rooted in what is to be abandoned by cultivation arises. Base-prenascence: the base … [and so on] …
A state with a root eradicated by cultivation is related to aggregates with roots eradicated by cultivation by way of prenascence condition.

A state with a root eradicated neither by seeing nor by cultivation is related to a state with a root eradicated by seeing and a state with a root eradicated neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of prenascence condition— namely, object-prenascence.
Base-prenascence. Object-prenascence: the eye ... [and so on] ... taking the base as object, doubt-accompanied aggregates and delusion arise.
Base-prenascence: the base is a condition, by way of prenascence-condition, for the doubt-accompanied aggregates and for delusion.

A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is a condition, by way of prenascence-condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation and for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation.
This is by way of object-prenascence and base-prenascence. Object-prenascence: the eye … [and so on] … having taken the base as object, restlessness-accompanied [states arise].
The aggregates and delusion arise. Basis-prenascence: the physical basis is a condition, by way of prenascence-condition, for the restlessness-accompanied aggregates and for delusion.
Postnascence...
A state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of posteriority condition, for a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by cultivation:
aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing, arising subsequently, are a condition,
by way of posteriority condition, for this preceding body.
A state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition, by way of posteriority condition, for a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation:
the aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation, arising subsequently, are a condition, by way of posteriority condition, for this body that has arisen previously.
A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is a condition,

by way of postnascence-condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation: postnascent aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation are a condition,
by way of postnascence-condition, for this prenascent body.

States whose roots are to be abandoned by vision and whose roots are neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation are related to a state whose roots are neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation by way of postnascence condition:
the postnascent aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are related to this prenascent body by way of postnascence condition.

States whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation and whose roots are neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation are related to a state whose root is neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation by way of postnascence condition:
the postnascent aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion are related to this prenascent body by way of postnascence condition.
A state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of the condition of repetition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing:
preceding aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing are [the condition] for succeeding aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing.

Aggregates whose causes are to be abandoned by seeing are related to aggregates whose causes are to be abandoned by seeing by way of the condition of repetition. A state whose cause is to be abandoned by seeing is related to a state whose cause is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by cultivation by way of the condition of repetition—
the preceding aggregates accompanied by doubt are related to the succeeding [aggregates].
Delusion is a condition for [subsequent states] by way of the condition of repetition.

A state rooted in factors to be abandoned by vision is a condition for a state both rooted in factors to be abandoned by vision and rooted in factors to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation,
by way of the condition of repetition— namely, preceding moments accompanied by doubt.
The preceding aggregates are related to the subsequent aggregates accompanied by doubt and to delusion by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).
A state with a root eradicated by cultivation is related to a state with a root eradicated by cultivation (abbreviated) in three ways.

A state with a root not eradicated either by seeing or by cultivation ... [etc. ... (In the section based on repetition, both emergence and adverting are to be eradicated; seventeen questions are complete, similar to the preceding.)
